\subsection*{Full Comparison: alg3\textunderscore{}LU vs PEG-BP}
% ==========================================

\medskip

\textbf{Key observations (binary).}
The alg3\textunderscore{}LU pruning decoder is consistently 2--6$\times$ faster than PEG-BP SPA at every error level where both succeed. At BER=3\%, alg3\textunderscore{}LU achieves $R=0.55$ (1100 information bits) while PEG only reaches $R=0.60$ (800~info~bits) --- meaning alg3\textunderscore{}LU carries \emph{more information with less redundancy} while decoding faster. PEG's sole advantage is at BER=4\%, where $R=0.60$ SPA still converges; alg3\textunderscore{}LU on genU matrices saturates at 4\% due to insufficient sure columns.

\medskip

\textbf{Non-binary fields.} GF(256)~$n=250$ is the fastest of all fields (0.022--0.039~ms), with $R=0.65$ uniquely reaching 5\%~SER --- higher noise tolerance than any binary PEG at 2000 columns. GF(16)~$n=500$ achieves rates as high as $R=0.88$ at 1\% error in under 0.2~ms, roughly 200$\times$ faster than PEG on the equivalent binary code. GF(4)~$n=1000$ is the most robust lower-rate performer: $R=0.55$ succeeds up to 4\%~SER, while higher rates ($R=0.60$--0.80) tolerate only 1--2\%.

\medskip

\textbf{Summary.}
The alg3\textunderscore{}LU decoder dominates PEG-BP in both speed and rate for low-to-moderate noise (BER $\leq$ 3\%). At higher noise (BER $\geq$ 4\%), PEG-BP with $R=0.60$ retains an edge on binary channels, but GF(256) at $R=0.65$ matches or exceeds this on a symbol-error channel. The extension to GF(16), GF(256), and GF(4) provides substantial flexibility for non-binary modulation schemes where PEG codes are unavailable.
